萬象/Writing 003

003 / Linguistics / Essay

Which Way Is Forward?

向前，怎麼到了後面？

Fast-forward to the later part. Look back at what came before. A small puzzle in Mandarin opens onto the many directions we give time.

Hoshikawa Miyu / 星川未有

Read / 閱讀
Contents 目次
  1. Forward to the later part往前快進，聽聽後面
  2. A queue of events, a road to walk一列事情，一條路
  3. Two days forward from Wednesday星期三往前兩天
  4. An hour ahead, an hour earlier他比我們早，還是比我們晚？
  5. A fast watch makes an early alarm錶快了，鬧鐘便早響了
  6. Arriving early, getting ahead早一點，便走到了前面
  7. The prequel written afterwards後來寫的前傳
  8. Forward to somewhere you have been按下前進，回到去過的地方
  9. Other places to put time時間還可以往哪裡放

01 / English

Forward to the later part

Halfway through a meeting, someone says, “We discussed that earlier; we’ll return to it later.” In Mandarin, the familiar words are 前面, the “front part,” and 後面, the “back part.” Nobody needs to turn around. The front is what we have already covered; the back is what we have yet to reach.

A little later, the same speaker says, “Let’s leave the past behind and look forward.” Mandarin has 向前看, too. The front, which just held the past, now holds the future.

A recording makes the trick especially neat:

往前快進一點，聽聽後面的內容。
Fast-forward a little and listen to the later part.

The instruction is perfectly usable. But line up the Chinese direction words and it becomes peculiar: why does going forward take us to the back part?

Reverse the instruction: go back a little and replay the earlier passage. Again, everyone knows what to do. Language performs the switch so smoothly that it takes a moment to notice anything has changed.

01 / 中文

往前快進，聽聽後面

會議開到一半，有人說：「這個前面說過，後面還會再談。」沒有人需要轉頭。 我們知道「前面」是已經講過的部分，「後面」是還沒講到的部分。

過了一會兒，同一個人又說：「過去的事就讓它過去，我們要向前看。」 剛才還裝著過去的「前」，忽然又裝進了未來。

錄音機把這件事表現得更乾脆：

往前快進一點，聽聽後面的內容。

這句話一點也不難懂。可是，把兩個方向詞並排放好，事情就有些奇怪了： 為甚麼往「前」走，反而到了「後」面？

我們也可以反過來說：「往後倒一點，重聽前面那句。」操作依然順利。 語言在這裡熟練得像一個魔術師，手法越自然，越不容易注意到它剛換過甚麼。

02 / English

A queue of events, a road to walk

Two small scenes help separate the directions.

In the first, events form a queue: opening remarks, a report, discussion, and adjournment. The opening comes first; adjournment comes last. Mandarin 前言 (preface), 後記 (afterword), 前任 (predecessor), and 後任 (successor) fit this picture. Front and back locate members of an ordered sequence.

In the second, we walk along a road. The stretch already travelled lies behind us; the stretch still to come lies ahead. We can 回首往事, look back on the past, or 展望前途, look ahead to our prospects. Here the directions belong to the person facing along the road. Linguists distinguish reference to another event from reference to the self. (Yu, 2012)

Return to the recording. Its “back part” has a position in the whole sequence; “fast-forward” moves the playback position in its normal direction of travel. A single sentence can use both arrangements.

There is another distinction hiding inside “past” and “future.” Tomorrow, we can eat before the meeting. Yesterday, we may have talked after it. Before tomorrow’s meeting is still in the future; after yesterday’s meeting is still in the past. Earlier than an event and earlier than now are different relations. One analysis of Mandarin 前 and 後 accordingly puts sequential order at the centre of their temporal uses. (Yang, Sinha, and Filipovic, 2023)

This lets 前年, the year before last, coexist with 前途, one’s prospects. A word such as 前年 alone cannot tell us which way a Mandarin speaker imagines facing. Experiments that separate event order from past–future judgments have found support for distinct reference frames. (Xiao, Zhao, and Chen, 2018)

02 / 中文

一列事情，一條路

先把一句話拆成兩個場景。

在第一個場景裡，事情排成一列：開場、報告、討論、散會。開場在前，散會在後。 「前言」「後記」「前任」「後任」都容易放進這幅圖裡。這種前後給序列中的 成員安排位置。

在第二個場景裡，我們沿著一條路走。已經走過的留在身後，還要走的在前方。 於是可以「回首往事」，也可以「展望前途」。這種前後以人的朝向為參照。 語言學中的一個重要區分，正是以事件為參照和以自我為參照。 （Yu，2012）

回到錄音：「後面的內容」標出它在整段錄音中的位置；「往前快進」描述播放 位置沿正常播放方向推進。兩個說法各自工作，一句話就能把它們接在一起。

還有一點很容易被「過去／未來」掩蓋。試看：

明天開會前，我們先吃飯。
昨天散會後，我們又聊了一會兒。

第一句的「前」仍在未來，第二句的「後」仍在過去。「早於某件事」和「早於 現在」是兩種不同的關係。關於漢語「前／後」的研究，也有從事件的先後次序 出發分析其時間用法的主張。（Yang、Sinha 與 Filipovic，2023）

因此，「前年」和「前途」可以共存；光看「前年」，也無法斷定一個漢語使用者 在想像中究竟朝向哪裡。區分事件次序與過去、未來的實驗，確實為這兩種參照 提供了支持。（Xiao、Zhao 與 Chen，2018）

03 / English

Two days forward from Wednesday

Sometimes the intended frame is harder to recover. Pick a new date for this meeting before opening the answer:

Next Wednesday’s meeting has been moved forward two days.

Monday or Friday?

Compare the two readings

Move the meeting toward the front of the schedule and it lands on Monday. Move it two days further in the direction of travel toward the future and it lands on Friday. Researchers have recorded both answers. The example shows how a single instruction can invite different interpretations.

This question has been used in research on spatial and temporal reference. The wording matters: translating it into Mandarin with 提前, “make earlier,” already selects Monday and removes the original ambiguity. (Bender and colleagues, 2012; Xiao and colleagues, 2018)

Other contrasts need no ambiguous instruction. To bring a meeting forward is to make it earlier; to put the clocks forward is to give the clocks a later reading. (Meeting usage; clock usage)

Operation Starting position New position
Bring a meeting forward an hour 3 p.m. 2 p.m.
Put a clock forward an hour Displays 2 p.m. Displays 3 p.m.
Fast-forward a recording a minute Plays at 02:00 Plays at 03:00

An appointment, a clock reading, and a playback position can all be moved. Before comparing their directions, we need to know which one we are moving.

03 / 中文

星期三往前兩天

不過，參照並不總能自動對齊。先讀這句英文，替會議選一個新日期：

Next Wednesday’s meeting has been moved forward two days.

是星期一，還是星期五？

選好之後，再看兩種讀法

若把會議往日程中較前的位置移，它從星期三移到星期一；若沿著自己走向未來的方向把會議移遠兩天，它便到了星期五。相關研究記錄了這兩種回答。這裡展示的是一句話如何容許不同理解。

這個題目已被用於時間與空間參照的研究；它也提醒我們，動詞和具體措辭會 影響理解。把它直接譯成「會議提前兩天」，中文的「提前」已經替讀者選好了 星期一，原來的歧義便消失了。 （Bender 等，2012；Xiao 等，2018）

有些對照甚至不需要歧義。英語的 bring a meeting forward 是把會議提前， put the clocks forward 卻是把鐘表撥到較晚的讀數。 （會議用法；鐘表用法）

操作 原來的位置 調整之後
會議提前一小時 下午三點 下午兩點
鐘表撥快一小時 顯示兩點 顯示三點
錄音快進一分鐘 播到 02:00 播到 03:00

日程上的約定、鐘面上的讀數、錄音裡的播放位置，都能被移動。開始比較方向 以前，得先知道手裡正在移哪一樣東西。

04 / English

An hour ahead, an hour earlier

Arranging a call with a friend abroad, we might say 他比我們早一個小時, literally “he is an hour earlier than us,” or 他在我們前邊, “he is ahead of us.” Suppose we are in Hong Kong and our friend is in Tokyo. Hong Kong uses UTC+8; Japan Standard Time is UTC+9. (Hong Kong Observatory; NICT, Japan)

At the same instant, our clock reads eight and his reads nine. His clock shows the larger number and the later time. Where does “earlier” enter the picture?

Give both places the same target: nine in the morning, local time. When Tokyo reaches nine, Hong Kong is still at eight and has an hour to wait for its own nine.

What we compare Hong Kong Tokyo
Clock readings at the same instant 08:00 09:00
Local 09:00 on the same date, expressed in UTC 01:00 00:00

At the same instant, it shows a later time; reaching the same clock reading, it gets there earlier. “Ahead” can follow the readings; “earlier” can follow the arrival at a common mark. New Year makes this vivid: Tokyo counts down the last ten seconds while Hong Kong still has another hour to wait.

“The time there is earlier” therefore needs context. “It is only seven there and already eight here” compares simultaneous readings. “They welcome the new year earlier” compares the arrivals at two local midnights. Earlier does different work in the two sentences.

04 / 中文

他比我們早，還是比我們晚？

和外地的朋友約通話時，我們可能會說：「他比我們早一個小時」，或者「他在 我們前邊」。假設我們在香港，朋友在東京：香港採用 UTC+8，日本標準時間是 UTC+9，兩地相差一小時。（香港天文台；日本 NICT）

同一瞬間，我們的鐘顯示八點，他的鐘顯示九點。他的鐘面數字比較大，顯示的 時刻比較晚。「早一個小時」的說法又從哪裡來？

把兩邊的目標都設成「當地上午九點」，就看得清楚了。東京已經到九點時， 香港才八點，還要等一小時才輪到自己的九點。

比較甚麼 香港 東京
同一瞬間，各自的鐘面讀數 08:00 09:00
同一天當地 09:00，換算成 UTC 01:00 00:00

在同一瞬間，它顯示較晚的時刻；要到達同一個鐘面時刻，它又比我們先到。 「在我們前邊」可以順著讀數理解，「比我們早」則可以順著某個共同刻度何時 到達來理解。跨年尤其直觀：東京已在倒數最後十秒，香港還要再等一小時。

這也解釋了為甚麼「那邊時間比較早」需要上下文。如果它的意思是「那邊現在 才七點，我們已經八點」，比較的是此刻的讀數；若說「那邊比我們早迎來新年」， 比較的便是兩地抵達各自零點的先後。兩句話裡的「早」做著不同的事。

05 / English

A fast watch makes an early alarm

The colloquial Mandarin 錶早了, roughly “the watch is early,” invites us to restore the missing comparison. Does it display an earlier time, or would following it make us act too early?

Suppose it is really 8:50, but a watch already reads 9:00. It is ten minutes fast and displays a later time. An alarm set for nine on that watch will ring ten minutes before the correct nine. Conversely, a watch displaying 8:50 at the real nine has an earlier reading and is ten minutes slow.

“My watch was fast, so I arrived early” and “my watch was slow, so I arrived late” both make sense. The direction of the error in the display reverses when we act on it. As with time zones, we can hold the instant fixed and compare readings, or hold the reading fixed and compare when it is reached.

Even “fast” needs a scale. “Five minutes fast” describes the present error; “gains five minutes a day” describes how the error grows. A watch set five minutes ahead can subsequently keep perfect time and remain five minutes fast without continuing to run faster.

05 / 中文

錶快了，鬧鐘便早響了

「錶早了」也值得把省略的部分補回來：是錶上顯示的時刻比較早，還是按照它 行動會太早？

假設實際才八點五十分，一隻錶已顯示九點。它快了十分鐘，顯示較晚的時刻； 若鬧鐘按這隻錶的九點響，就會比正確的九點早響十分鐘。反過來，實際九點 卻只顯示八點五十分的錶，讀數較早，是慢了十分鐘。

於是，「錶快了，所以我來早了」和「錶慢了，所以我來晚了」都很自然。 鐘面上的早晚與照著它行動的早晚，恰好反向。和時區一樣，我們可以固定 同一瞬間比較讀數，也可以固定同一讀數比較它何時到達。

連「快」也有兩種尺度。「快了五分鐘」說的是目前差多少；「每天快五分鐘」 說的才是誤差怎樣增長。一隻被人撥快五分鐘、此後走得完全準的錶，可以一直 「快五分鐘」，卻沒有一直走得更快。

06 / English

Arriving early, getting ahead

“She finished early, so she is ahead of schedule.” Another crossing hides in this unremarkable sentence.

Imagine two people reading the same book. On Wednesday, Lin is at chapter three and Zhou has reached chapter five. Chapter five comes after chapter three, but Zhou is ahead of Lin. She has reached on Wednesday a place he will not reach until Friday.

There are two quantities here: a date and a stage of progress. Being ahead means reaching a later stage at an earlier time. As on a running track, an earlier arrival and a greater distance travelled can describe the same achievement.

“Ahead of its time” extends the route further. We expect a technology to become common in the future; someone produces it today, and we call it ahead of the age. Mandarin 思想超前 and 技術落後 do similar work for ideas and technology. Direction acquires an evaluation: calling something “behind” often carries an assumption about where we think it ought to go.

06 / 中文

早一點，便走到了前面

「他提前完成，所以進度領先。」這句話裡藏著另一種交叉。

假設兩個人讀同一本書。星期三，小林讀到第三章，小周已經讀到第五章。 第五章排在第三章後面，小周卻走在小林前面。小林要到星期五才讀到的地方， 小周星期三就到了。

這裡同時有一個日期和一個進度。在較早的時間，到達較後的階段，便成了 「領先」。就像同一條跑道上，先到的人走得更遠：日曆上的早，與路程上的遠， 可以描述同一項成績。

「思想超前」「技術落後」又把這條路延伸了出去。我們預想某種技術將來才會 普及，今天有人先做出來，就說它走在時代前面。「前」於是既涉及時間，也帶著 對發展方向的判斷。一件東西被叫作「落後」，往往已經包含了我們希望它往哪裡走。

07 / English

The prequel written afterwards

Stories add more sequences. Imagine an author writing a character’s adult adventures, then returning years later to write about her childhood. The new book is a prequel: later in publication, earlier in the character’s life.

A reader might begin with the childhood book, then read the adult adventures. The reading order now differs from the publication order. We can arrange at least three things in sequence: the publication of the books, the events they narrate, and the reader’s encounters with them.

A film can do the same within one work. At minute ten, the character is an adult; at minute twenty, a flashback takes us to childhood. We fast-forward to a later part of the film and arrive at an earlier part of the story. “Skip ahead” is easy for the player to carry out. “See what happens later” leaves a question: later in the telling, or later in the character’s life?

Forward, later, and earlier can all fit the same move. Each points to a different ordering.

07 / 中文

後來寫的前傳

故事讓事情更熱鬧了。想像一位作者先寫主角成年後的冒險，幾年後又補寫他的 童年。這部新作是一部「前傳」：出版得較晚，講的事卻較早。

如果讀者先看童年篇，再看成年篇，閱讀次序又跟出版次序分了家。同一套作品， 至少有三種可以逐一排列的東西：出版的作品、敘述的事件，以及讀者翻開書的經歷。

一部電影也能如此。第十分鐘還在講成年生活，第二十分鐘突然回到童年。 我們往前快進，到了影片後面的段落，卻看見故事裡更早的事。此時若有人說 「跳到後面」，播放器很容易照做；若說「看看後來發生了甚麼」，得先弄清楚 他說的是影片怎樣接著演，還是角色的人生怎樣接著過。

「往前」「後面」「更早」在這裡可以全都成立。它們分別指著不同的排列。

08 / English

Forward to somewhere you have been

A browser puts several of these orders behind two small arrows.

Suppose we visit pages A, B, and C, then press Back to return to B. Pressing Forward takes us to C again. The page “ahead” is somewhere we have already been.

Think of the stored history as a row of positions: A → B → C. The selected position moves from C to B and back to C. Meanwhile, our actual experience unfolds as A, B, C, B, C. We can move either way through the stored history; each new click still follows the previous one.

Undo and Redo have the same charm. Redo restores a state the document has already had, but the act of restoring it is new. The computer lets us select an earlier state again, in the present.

The Forward button can therefore take us back to familiar ground.

08 / 中文

按下前進，回到去過的地方

瀏覽器把這幾種次序放到了兩個小箭頭上。

假設我們依次看了 A、B、C 三個網頁，再按「後退」回到 B。現在按「前進」， 就會再次看到 C。這個在「前方」的網頁，明明剛才已經看過。

可以把訪問記錄想成一列固定的位置：A → B → C。目前選中的位置從 C 回到 B， 再移到 C。與此同時，我們真正經歷的順序卻是 A、B、C、B、C。歷史記錄裡的 位置可以往返，每一次按鍵仍接在上一次之後。

「撤銷」和「重做」也有同樣的趣味。重做讓文件回到曾經有過的狀態，這次重做 本身卻是剛發生的新操作。電腦沒有把我們送回過去；它讓我們現在重新選中 一個過去的狀態。

所以，按鈕上的「前進」甚至可以通往已經走過的地方。

09 / English

Other places to put time

Once we start looking, more spatial words appear.

Mandarin 上個月 and 下個月 put last month “up” and next month “down.” 遠古 and 遙遠的未來 make both antiquity and the future distant. “The holiday is approaching” sets the event in motion; “we’re approaching the end of the year” sets us moving instead. Even 眼前, “before the eyes,” can hold either an immediate problem or a childhood scene appearing in memory.

Direction, distance, movement, and visibility each contribute something. The front–back axis is one arrangement among several, though a particularly easy one to take for granted.

Aymara offers a revealing comparison. Núñez and Sweetser identified a pattern in language and gesture placing the past in front of the person and the future behind. One explanation they discuss connects the known past with what is visible in front, and the unknown future with what cannot be seen behind. Visibility supplies a different basis for the arrangement. A future in front of us begins to look like one possibility among others. (Núñez and Sweetser, 2006)

In such comparisons, both words and gestures matter. A couple of expressions alone give us too little evidence to draw one shared map of time for everyone who speaks a language.

09 / 中文

時間還可以往哪裡放

沿著這條線再找下去，還能找到一整組空間詞。

「上個月／下個月」給月份排了上下；「遠古／遙遠的未來」把「遠」同時用在 現在的兩側；「春節快到了」讓節日走近我們，「我們快走到年底了」又讓我們 自己走起來。連「眼前」也很靈活：眼前可以有待處理的困難，也可以浮現童年 的往事。

這些說法中，方向、距離、移動和可見性各自提供了一點幫助。前後軸只是其中 最容易被我們當成理所當然的一條。

艾馬拉語提供了一個特別值得比較的例子。Núñez 與 Sweetser 的研究在語言與 手勢中辨認出一種把過去放在人的前方、未來放在後方的模式。他們討論的一種 解釋是：已知的過去像眼前可見的東西，未知的未來則像身後看不見的東西。 這個解釋把重點放在可見性上。它也讓「人的前方自然就是未來」不再顯得是 唯一的選擇。（Núñez 與 Sweetser，2006）

在這類比較裡，詞語和手勢都值得看；一兩個詞本身，還不足以替整個語言的 使用者畫出一張共同的時間地圖。

10 / English

Now look back at the earlier part

By now, the opening of this essay lies behind you in the experience of reading. To revisit it, you can scroll up or choose an earlier heading in the contents. Then you can move forward again, reading down toward the later passages.

A small journey through a page recruits several directions. Usually they cooperate so well that we hardly stop to notice which events form the sequence, which position is moving, or whose way of facing supplies the orientation.

At the next meeting, someone may say, “Earlier we looked back at the past; later we’ll look forward.” The Mandarin version neatly puts 前面, 後面, and 向前看 into one sentence. Perhaps it will distract you for a second. The speaker has not turned around. A few ordinary words have quietly changed the reference frame.

As for further examples—we can get to those later. 後面再說。

10 / 中文

現在，回頭看看前面

讀到這裡，文章前面的內容已經在閱讀經驗中落到了身後。要回頭看它，可以 往上捲，也可以按一下目次裡排在前面的標題。如果返回後再繼續往下讀，我們 又會向前推進，讀到文章後面的部分。

只是在頁面上來回看了兩眼，就用上了好幾種方向。平常它們配合得很好，於是 我們很少停下來辨認：這一次排的是哪一列事情，移的是哪一個位置，又是誰 朝著哪裡看。

下次會議裡聽到「前面我們回顧了過去，後面我們要向前看」，或許會稍微分心 一秒鐘。說話的人沒有轉身，時間也沒有倒流，幾個熟悉的詞已經替我們換好了 參照。

至於還能找到甚麼例子——我們後面再說。
